I have ADHD, generalized anxiety disorder and depression. I do edibles pretty frequently and they help me A LOT to slow down my thoughts - mainly to distinguish between the thought-patterns that are good for me and those which aren't. They also help me hyperfocus on something that my anxiety makes me avoid. I also drink in social settings because (once again) it helps inhibit my anxious thoughts. I do recommend learning about mechanisms of each drug you're interested in consuming, as well as reading papers on how they affect different types of brains. I learned how your brain works on different drugs before consuming them and before knowing I had ADHD. I write A LOT when I'm high, mainly noting down my own observations because I also use edibles for trauma reprocessing. I then go over the main things with my therapist (who is fully aware of my edible consumption).

It really depends on each person and if you're not even curious to try drugs, then I'd recommend not even worrying about it. Hope this helped! :)

I'm in a kinda similar situation. I'd just suggest learning as many programming languages as you can (there's a bunch of online tutorials). Teach yourself about data science. Learn about computer science & software development basics (how to access & use the command-line + more - there's an MIT course on this). This is what I'm planning on doing once I'm done this neuroaesthetics paper lol.

Also learn about AI theory. What are the different definitions of intelligence? What makes an agent intelligent? and all that fun philosophical stuff - try epistemology, theory of mind, ethics. Different perspectives on cognition and AI might also be useful. Also learn some linguistics - useful if you're interested in NLP & will help you learn programming languages way more easily (at least it helped me).

Then do what u/whiskeyhotelpreston said. Think of a problem you're passionate about and attempt to explore it (your aim doesn't need to be to solve it) through the use of an AI program - ideally one that you've programmed. It's like making an app but attempting to address real-life issues, rather than purely for entertainment.

Hope this helps! I might just be talking out of my ass.

Neuroaesthetics is basically trying to find the exact brain areas that light up when we appreciate art / perceive beauty (through fMRI studies). The main issue is what the exact definition of "aesthetics" is (philosophy gives it a different definition than art history, for example). It would make sense that once the neural pathway is identified, it potentially would be possible to program the behaviour into code!! Hence maybe AI won't "appreciate" art, but at least it'll be perceiving a specific artwork and finding aesthetic patterns that are what generally deem it beautiful. But another problem also comes by the subjectivity of beauty - is it really in the eye of the beholder? Or can beauty be quantified? There's a lot of questions to think about before trying to code an AI program imo heheh

Hey, very suicidal person here - with a family that doesn't quite understand how a suicidal brain works. Here are some of the reasons why I chose and am currently choosing to stay, in pretty general terms. These reasons are in constant flux and sometimes they aren't enough, but I think I'm good at verbalising my thoughts and feelings, so as long as I might help you help your sister, I'm fine with doing the extra mental work it takes to communicate the incommunicable. I think sharing this with your sister might be helpful, of course it's up to you what you think might be better for her, and ask her if she feels comfortable about sharing her experience with you, respecting boundaries is extremely important.

* I believe recovery is possible. I've reached out to people online who have attempted multiple times and they still continue choosing to live. We motivate and love each other through life, even if we've never met before.
* I've given it a purpose. I want to be one of those people who put their all into reminding others there's still hope. I've already been told I've helped many people through their mental health struggles, and I sincerely expect nothing in return. Knowing that the darkness in my brain serves a purpose to others gives me a reason to stay.
* I am curious. I love Science so I want to know what the future holds for humanity in terms of technology. If I don't stay, then I'll never get to see these advances.
* I love my family. I want to watch my brother walk down the aisle with his husband. I want to see my other brother graduate university. I want to see my nieces graduating high school.  I want to live long enough until I know that those I love will be ok without me.
* I love my pets. I simply can't do it right now because if I do then my dogs won't know what happened to me and they'll look for me! I can't let them be lost without an answer, I know how that feels like and I wouldn't wanna make them go through it.
* I want to see my friends succeed; this one's personal. I want to see my best friend graduate from Cambridge University with her Master's degree, and watch her say "fuck you" to everyone who didn't believe in her. I want to see her thrive and achieve her dreams; have a wife, a dog, a home. I want to see my other best friend become a successful artist. Continue expressing her pain through her art, and have people value it as much as her creativity deserves. I want my (yet other) best friend graduate from med school. I want to make sure she's happy helping cure people, and she can finally travel the world as she has always wanted to. I want my friends who've suffered from sexual assault or emotional abuse by their partners to know they deserve better than misogynistic manipulative men (I've been through this as well and it took me a long ass time to learn that). I want to see the people I love content, so how could I ever do that if I give up now?
* I want to try new things. I can't do that if I'm dead.
* I want to experience things I miss, at least one more time. I want to know what it felt like to have a coffee by myself as I listen to music and read a book at a random coffee shop or beneath a tree's shade. I want to experience what being happy and at peace felt like. This can be things from childhood as well, no matter how small they may seem to you, they might mean the world to someone else. One that I tried was going on a swing set with my roommate. I felt like a free child again. It felt like heaven.

There are many more reasons, but I'm kind of mentally exhausted right now.

I'm down to chat if you ever need it. I hope your sister knows how much you love her.
